column1: # entropy_coder_cshape_2026-09-05 — the entropy coefficient writer, the range
# coder and the pack-side eob scan taken to C's SHAPE.
# base = main@origin e622a99c2, host r7900x (x86_64-linux, AMD Ryzen 9 7900X).
# Every build below writes byte-identical .obu on every cell listed.
#   A  pipeline.rs: the three forward full-block eob scans -> reverse scan with
#   B  range_coder.rs: `encode_cdf_q15` fused to C's single-predicate shape and
#      `normalize` split into an `#[inline]` hot path + `#[cold]` flush.
#   C  coeff_c.rs: C's `eob == 1` fast path in `write_coeffs_txb_1d`.  REVERTED.
#   D  cdf.rs: `update_cdf` split into C's two branchless loops.  REVERTED.
#   E  coeff_c.rs: the writer's `[0i8; 32*32]` -> the (unused) TxbScratch::ctx.
#   F  coeff_c.rs: the `c == eob - 1` iteration peeled out of the backward loop.
# branch-misses:u`, `taskset -c 20` on BOTH sides, paired warmup-delta (two
# warmup levels, the delta is N encodes' worth so process setup / .yuv read /
# .obu write cancel exactly), MEDIAN OF 5 REPETITIONS, normalised to ONE encode.
# An EARLIER session measured chunk A ALONE against the same base (a separate
# pair of runs; the base row is that session's own base, not the one above).
# AB — `tools/perf_ab.sh`, 21 interleaved paired rounds per cell, order
# randomised per round, NEITHER side niced, every row ident=Y. `ratio` is
# cand/base per-frame encode time (median of the per-round paired ratios);
# `speedup` = base/cand. The CONTROL rows run the SAME BINARY on both sides.
# An EARLIER grid measured chunk A ALONE (base vs candA) on the same host,
# before B and F existed: photo_cid p6 0.9791/1.021, p2 1.0074/0.993;
# gradient 512 p6 1.0014/0.999, p2 1.0036/0.996. No base-vs-base control was
# taken for that grid — its p2 rows are the reason one was run at all.
# PORTFN — per-function SELF numbers from the same callgrind runs
# (callgrind_annotate, photo_cid 512² p6). `flush` does not exist in base/candA
# and `normalize` does not exist in candF: that is the split, visible.
# MEM — peak RSS (`/usr/bin/time -v` "Maximum resident set size"), x86-64
# r7900x, gradient 2048x2048 qp 40 preset 13, 5 repetitions, KiB. The still and
# inter cells' .obu are byte-identical between the two binaries (the inter one
# at 139,761 B, which is also a byte-identity data point on the 2048 inter
# path). RSS, not heap: it counts every page the allocator ever touched.
